title: Abu Simbel
standfirst: The two rock-cut temples of Ramesses II at Abu Simbel stand on the shore of Lake Nasser, south of Aswan. Most visitors come on a day trip from Aswan. It is one of the places in our guide to [[up]].

sections.heading: The temples
paragraphs: The Great Temple, with its four colossal seated statues of Ramesses II, and the smaller temple of his queen, Nefertari. In the 1960s both were cut into blocks and moved higher up, away from the rising waters of the new lake.

sections.heading: Getting there
paragraphs: Abu Simbel is a long drive south from Aswan, about three to four hours each way, usually leaving before dawn. There are also short flights. Many cruises offer it as an optional excursion on the day in Aswan.

sections.heading: The sun festival
paragraphs: Twice a year, around 22 February and 22 October, the rising sun reaches the inner sanctuary of the Great Temple. Those days are very busy.

faqs.q: How do I get to Abu Simbel from Aswan?
faqs.a: By road, about three to four hours each way, or by a short flight. Our Abu Simbel day trip goes by road.

faqs.q: Is Abu Simbel worth the trip?
faqs.a: For most visitors, yes: the temples are among the most striking in Egypt.

seoDescription: The temples of Abu Simbel, how they were moved, how to get there from Aswan and when the sun reaches the sanctuary.
